power_purchase.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, considering the approved distribution loss of 10.00%, the Commission hereby approves the power purchase cost as Rs.2661.77 lakh for the year 2021-22 as against as 2694.19 lakh claimed in the petition.
key_observations: actual distribution loss is higher than the approved level of distribution loss
quantum of power purchased corresponding to the excess distribution loss shall be disallowed
power_purchase.methodology_applied: approved distribution loss of 10.00% for the year 2021-22

employee_cost.kserc_reasoning: Therefore, the Commission hereby allows Rs.23.65 lakh towards wage revision in addition to the amount approved in ARR Order dated 11-11-2019 as per the provisions of Tariff Regulations. 2018. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves the employee expenses of Rs.169.31 lakh (145.66+23.65) for the year 2021-22 against the licensee's claim of Rs.172.12 lakh.
key_observations: impact of triennial wage revision for workers amounting to Rs.23.65 lakh
increase was not reflected in the norms approved by the Commission

repair_maintenance.kserc_reasoning: As the Commission had approved Rs.48.55 lakh towards R&M expenses while truing up the accounts for the year 2020-21, the commission is inclined to approve R&M expenses for the year 2021-22 by applying the escalation factor of 4.84 %. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves the R&M expenses of Rs.50.90 lakh (48.55+4.84%) for the year 2021-22. The Commission would however advice the licensee to maintain the reliability and quality of their service and must take timely action to ensure the same.
key_observations: various items of expenses incurred for R&M works were of routine maintenance expense and there is no one-time expense which can be allowed over and above the norm
repair_maintenance.methodology_applied: applying the escalation factor of 4.84 % to 2020-21 trued up amount

admin_general.kserc_reasoning: The licensee in the truing up petition claimed Rs.2.37 lakh as Legal Charges incurred towards fee and expenses paid to the advocates to file appeal before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity against the orders of KSERC. During the previous year also, the licensee claimed similar expenses and the Commission has taken a consistent stand that the expenses incurred towards legal proceedings cannot be charged to the A&G expenses unless there is an order from the respective Courts regarding payment of costs. Hence this amount of Rs.2.37 lakh is disallowed by the Commission. Based on the details furnished by the licensee, the Commission hereby approves Rs.14.96 lakh as the A&G expenses for the year 2021-22.
key_observations: expenses incurred towards legal proceedings cannot be charged to the A&G expenses unless there is an order from the respective Courts regarding payment of costs
admin_general.methodology_applied: Consistent stand from previous Truing up orders

depreciation.kserc_reasoning: After verifying the detailed calculations, the Commission hereby approves the depreciation of Rs.12.37 lakh for the year 2021-22 as shown below.

interest_long_term.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the interest on normative loan approved by the Commission for the year 2021-22 is Rs.5.73 lakh.
interest_long_term.methodology_applied: Regulation 29(2) and 29(4) of the Tariff Regulations 2018

interest_working_capital.kserc_reasoning: Based on the approved O&M expenses and power purchase cost, the Commission approves Rs.28.43 lakh as interest on working capital for the year 2021-22 as worked out below:

key_observations: lower claim is on account of decrease in interest rate from 4.50% to 4.25%
interest_consumer_deposits.methodology_applied: actual interest paid on security deposit

key_observations: claim of Rs.3.92 lakh is towards the bank charges for opening the letter of credit to KSEB Ltd as per the power purchase agreement

key_observations: bank guarantee charges for the above purpose shall not be included in the allowable expenses

key_observations: licensee clarified that they paid the amount during the current year
prior_period_expense.methodology_applied: Payment made during the current year

return_on_nfa.kserc_reasoning: Adopting the same method of calculation, the Commission hereby approves Rs. 3.83 lakh as RoNFA for the year 2021-22 as tabulated below:
return_on_nfa.methodology_applied: same method of calculation as 2020-21 truing up

other_debits.kserc_reasoning: The Commission has not been admitting Section 3(1) Duty as a revenue expenditure since as per the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, the Electricity Duty under this Section on the sales of energy should be borne by the Licensee and shall not be passed on to the consumers. Hence, the Commission disallows the licensee's claim of Rs.12.95 lakh as Section 3(1) duty. Commission considers the same and approves Rs.1.13 lakh, the periodical inspection charges under other debits. Accordingly, the Commission after disallowing the claim under Section 3(1) duty, approves an amount of Rs.1.13 lakh as Other debits for the year 2021-22.
key_observations: Section 3(1) Duty under the Kerala Electricity Duty Act should be borne by the Licensee and shall not be passed on to the consumers
periodical inspection charges are approved

revenue_from_sale_of_power.kserc_reasoning: The same is to be considered as part of other operational income under Non-Tariff Income and is treated accordingly. As such, the Commission hereby approves the revenue from sale of power at Rs.2949.85 lakh for the purpose of Truing Up of Accounts for the year 2021-22.
key_observations: licensee has included revenue from other operations of Rs.5.63 lakh as part of Revenue from sale of power
revenue_from_sale_of_power.methodology_applied: Reclassification of other operational income to Non-Tariff Income

non_tariff_income.kserc_reasoning: Therefore, the Commission is approving Rs.14.84 lakh being the amount of interest on security deposit worked out by the licensee and Rs.5.33 lakh claimed by the licensee as miscellaneous recoveries. Considering this argument, the Commission hereby adjust the differential amount of Rs.0.90 lakh in the interest on accumulated surplus for the current year and approves the amount of Rs.47.87 lakh (48.77-0.90) as interest on accumulated surplus for the year 2021-22. Thus, the Commission approves a total Non-tariff income of Rs.71.25 lakh during the year 2021-22 as tabulated below.
key_observations: licensee has not considered the Interest on Deposit with KSEB as part of non-tariff income
Commission is approving Rs.14.84 lakh for interest on security deposit
Rs.5.33 lakh claimed as miscellaneous recoveries is approved
interest on accumulated surplus adjusted by Rs.0.90 lakh to Rs.47.87 lakh
Rs.2.42 lakh claimed as reversal of amount recovered from doubtful debts is approved
non_tariff_income.methodology_applied: Notional interest on accumulated revenue surplus at SBI retail term deposit rate (5.00%)
